m1_zero_omission_notes.chapter_executive_summary: Applies trigonometric ratios to measure real-world heights and distances using line of sight, angle of elevation (looking up), and angle of depression (looking down).

detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 9.1 Line of Sight, Angle of Elevation and Depression
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Line of sight: line from observer's eye to object. Angle of elevation: angle between horizontal line and line of sight above horizontal. Angle of depression: angle below horizontal.

margin_boxes_and_in_text_notes.full_content: Angle of depression from top of tower to ground point equals angle of elevation from ground point to top.

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: Angle formed by line of sight with horizontal when object is above horizontal level.

formulas_rules_and_laws.model_application_example: If tower height h = ?, dist = 10m, θ = 45° => tan 45° = h/10 => h = 10m.

m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.objective_or_aim: Determine height of school building without direct measurement.
step_by_step_procedure: Measure distance d from building base.
Use clinometer to read angle of elevation θ.
Calculate height h = d * tan θ.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.expected_observations_or_working: Combining angle measurement with simple trigonometry yields building height.

level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.question: A ladder against a wall makes angle 60° with ground. Foot is 2.5 m from wall. Find ladder length.
level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.model_answer: cos 60° = Adjacent / Hypotenuse => 1/2 = 2.5 / L => L = 5 m.

level_3_long_answer_and_reasoning_5_mark.question: As observed from top of 75 m lighthouse, angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. If one ship is exactly behind the other, find distance between ships.
level_3_long_answer_and_reasoning_5_mark.model_answer: Let lighthouse be AB = 75 m. Ship 1 at C (45°), Ship 2 at D (30°). In ΔABC: tan 45° = 75/BC => BC = 75 m. In ΔABD: tan 30° = 75/BD => 1/√3 = 75/BD => BD = 75√3 m. Distance CD = BD - BC = 75√3 - 75 = 75(√3 - 1) m ≈ 75(0.732) = 54.9 m.

m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.frequent_student_error: Measuring angle of depression from vertical instead of horizontal.
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.correct_approach: Angle of depression is ALWAYS measured from the horizontal line of sight downward.
